questions.stem: An astronaut on the Moon drops a metal tool. Another astronaut standing nearby cannot hear the impact. Why?

options.text: Sound travels too slowly on the Moon
The Moon's gravity is too weak to carry sound
There is no atmosphere on the Moon, and sound requires a medium to travel through
Sound only travels through solids, not through space suits

questions.explanation: Sound is a longitudinal mechanical wave that requires particles to transfer vibrations through compressions and rarefactions. The Moon has no atmosphere (essentially a vacuum), so there are no air particles to vibrate. Option D is wrong — sound can travel through solids, liquids, AND gases, but not through a vacuum.

questions.stem: A sound wave has a frequency of 256 Hz. The speed of sound in air is 340 m/s. What is the wavelength of this sound?
questions.explanation: Wavelength = v / f = 340 / 256 = 1.328 m, which rounds to 1.33 m. Option B (87,040) comes from multiplying v x f instead of dividing. Option C (0.75) comes from f / v. Always use wavelength = speed / frequency.

questions.stem: Two identical sound waves are produced. One has a higher pitch than the other. What property of the wave is different?

options.text: Amplitude
Speed
Frequency
Wavelength only, not frequency

questions.explanation: Pitch is determined by frequency — a higher frequency produces a higher pitch. Amplitude (option A) determines loudness, not pitch. Speed (option B) depends on the medium, not the sound itself. While wavelength does change with frequency (option D), it is the frequency that directly determines pitch.

questions.stem: Sound travels at 340 m/s in air and 1500 m/s in water. A whale makes a call underwater. What happens to the sound when it reaches the surface and enters the air?

options.text: It speeds up and the wavelength increases
It slows down and the wavelength decreases, but the frequency stays the same
It slows down, the frequency decreases, and the wavelength stays the same
It speeds up because air is less dense

questions.explanation: Sound travels faster in water (1500 m/s) than in air (340 m/s), so it slows down when entering air. The frequency is set by the source (the whale) and does not change. Since v = f x wavelength and f is constant while v decreases, the wavelength must also decrease. Option D is wrong — sound actually travels slower in less dense media like air.

questions.stem: A student uses an oscilloscope to display two different sounds. Sound A shows tall, closely-spaced waves. Sound B shows short, widely-spaced waves. Which comparison is correct?

options.text: Sound A is quiet and low-pitched
Sound A is loud and high-pitched
Sound B is loud and high-pitched
Both sounds have the same loudness but different pitches

questions.explanation: Tall waves on an oscilloscope mean large amplitude (loud sound). Closely-spaced waves mean high frequency (short period), which corresponds to high pitch. Sound A is therefore loud and high-pitched. Sound B, with short (small amplitude) and widely-spaced (low frequency) waves, would be quiet and low-pitched. Students often confuse amplitude (height) with frequency (spacing).
